seen.extent: One printed facsimile page of about 17 lines of symbol text, about 200 px wide in the blog copy; the Saturday Evening Post issue itself was not found or opened.
seen.cipher: Monoalphabetic symbol substitution (hearts, bars, crosses, dots), Spanish plaintext; Yardley prints 'que' as a hint. No decipherment is printed on the page (the pencil ticks and '900 QUE' are annotations on this reader's copy).

prior_art.edition: Issue of the Saturday Evening Post not identified (Yardley's 1931 series); no printed solution found by web search.
prior_art.literature: Schmeh blog 24 Feb 2019: commenters Norbert, Tony and Thomas give a Spanish reading ('Hace tres dias que estoy en esta simpatica hacienda ... imborrables recuerdos ... detalles ...'), symbols for rr and ch proposed; Thomas offers a fuller reading with unresolved letters. The comments were read only in summary.

1306.key_check: No key held in the repo; a simple symbol substitution has no external key. The commenters' readings were not tested here because the symbols are only visible at about 200 px and the Post original is not found.
1306.duplicates: known.py run for 'Saturday Evening Post' and 'Yardley': only the lead itself and unrelated NARA/Mauborgne entries; the other Yardley cryptogram on the same blog page (American Black Chamber, 1931) is a different text.
1306.closed: Read in blog comments (Spanish, Norbert/Tony/Thomas 2019) but never confirmed as a complete plaintext; a simple-substitution training puzzle, not an archival cipher; promote only as a transcription check if wanted.

seen.where: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sitio-barcelona-1714-carta-codigo-cifrado.jpg (1055x887 px, AHCB Consell de Cent Cartas 1B-X-127)
seen.extent: Recto and verso side by side: about 22 lines of 2-digit number runs on the left page, a 10-line cipher passage on the right, signed 'El Marques del Poal' (Antoni Desvalls), dated 1714.
seen.cipher: Numeric code of 2-digit groups (about 11-50) with separators. Letters are written above many number runs (fragments such as 'rubi', 'tindr', 'embarasarme', 'Villarroel' are visible), i.e. an interlinear decipherment of unknown date and hand is on the leaf; whether it covers every line could not be judged.

prior_art.literature: No article on its cipher found; Dovella and Pedralbes articles on Poal's August-September 1714 movements give context only.

1246.key_check: No Austriacist 1714 key is held in the repo; the visible interlinear letters act as a partial key but 1055 px is too coarse to transcribe the number-letter pairs reliably, so no key was tested.

1246.closed: The leaf carries an interlinear decipherment above many number runs, so it is not a blank cryptogram; completeness cannot be judged at 1055 px. Reopen only with an AHCB hi-res scan.
